faq_slots.question: Why does water sit on my patio or lawn after rain?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words: ground underneath that drains slowly, a surface that falls the wrong way, no drain or soakaway to take the water. Then what the local ground adds, then the fix.

faq_slots.question: Is it better to lay turf or sow grass seed?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Turf gives a usable lawn sooner; seed costs less and suits larger areas but takes longer to establish. Timing matters for both.

faq_slots.question: What is the best time of year to landscape a garden?
faq_slots.answer_brief: When each kind of work goes in and why, in the soil or the plant, from the trade facts timing cells: paving and groundwork wait for ground that is neither frozen nor sodden, because a base cannot be firmed when it is wet; turf, seed and planting go in while the soil is warm and moist so the roots take before heat or frost. Nothing about spring being busy or booking ahead. No dates, no promise about the weather.

faq_slots.question: Will my patio or driveway need planning permission?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Point at the trade facts rule rows (Table C) and write what usually applies, with "usually" or "in most cases": a patio in the back garden usually needs none; a new surface at the front of the house usually needs the rain to soak away inside the garden; a raised deck or a structure near a boundary is where a rule can come in. What the customer does about it only as the row gives it. No figure, no area, no height, never an Act's or an order's name. Conservation areas and listed homes add controls: say so without naming them.

B.question: How often do you need to come?
B.answer_brief: What decides it, in plain words: grass and hedges grow fastest from spring to midsummer as the soil warms and slow right down in the cold months and in a dry spell, so the gap between visits follows the growth (the trade facts timing cells). A frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; otherwise say the pattern is agreed with you and nothing more. Never promise a schedule; a seasonal contract only when confirmed.

B.question: What does a regular visit cover?
B.answer_brief: The jobs on the card list said as one visit: the lawn and its edges, the beds, the hedge when it is in its cutting window. What a visit does not cover only from the services list. Nothing about design or projects unless the services list has them: a maintenance client's copy never implies design work. Link one service page where LINKABLE PAGES has one.

cards.title: A garden with nowhere to sit out
cards.brief: A situation card, not a fault: the household looks at the garden from the house and has nowhere flat and dry for a table and chairs, to let the children out or to stand with a coffee. What decides it: the levels and the ground by the back door (a slope, a lawn that stays wet, a step down to nothing). What the work gives them, in plain words: a patio or a deck made the size they will use, a level lawn, steps that make the lower garden reachable. By category: Paving reads it as the patio and its base; Decking as the deck, where the evening sun falls and what holds it up; Landscape Gardener as whichever fits the garden; Tree Service as the one sunny corner shaded out by a tree that has grown over it, and what lifting or thinning the crown gives back. Never a lifestyle pitch, never a fault invented for it.
cards.mechanism: no level, dry place to sit near the house

cards.title: Slabs, boards or posts that move underfoot
cards.brief: Problem led: a slab that rocks, blocks that have dipped, a deck board that gives, a post that leans, a young tree that rocks in its stake. The one cause this card makes: what holds it up was never made firm (a sub base not compacted, a subframe on soft supports, a post set shallow, a tree staked loosely), so the ground or the frame gives under it. Say what a sound base, footing or support involves in plain words from the trade facts stages, and that the fix starts underneath, not on top. By category: Paving reads it in the base under slabs and blocks; Decking in the joists, posts and supports; Tree Service in the stake, the planting pit or a stump left under a surface; Landscape Gardener in steps, paths and walls. No depth or figure the rows do not give.
cards.mechanism: what holds it up was never made firm

cards.title: Rain that stays where it lands
cards.brief: Problem led: puddles that sit on paving after rain, a deck green and slippery by autumn, a corner of lawn soft for days, a planting hole that fills with water. The one cause this card makes: a surface laid with no fall, so the rain cannot run off it. Say what the fix usually involves (a fall built into the laying, a base that drains, timber kept off wet ground, a tree planted at the right level) from the trade facts stages; what the business does on site only from confirmed practices. Never promise the ground will change. By category: Paving reads it on the surface; Decking in boards and joists that never dry; Tree Service in a tree standing in ground that holds water; Landscape Gardener across the garden. Not slow draining ground on its own: the symptom FAQ may own that.
cards.mechanism: a surface laid with no fall

cards.title: Planted or built for a different garden
cards.brief: A situation and a warning sign in one: borders now hard against the path, a drive too small for the cars that use it, a deck in the corner the sun left years ago, a tree planted close to the house that now reaches the roof. The one cause this card makes: planting and levels set years ago for a different garden. Say how looking at the whole garden before pricing one part of it works, from confirmed practices only. By category: Landscape Gardener reads it as layout and levels; Paving as the front garden and the drive; Decking as a platform in the wrong place or at the wrong height; Tree Service as the warning signs in the tree itself (branches rubbing the building, deadwood showing, a damaged limb, from the trade facts signs row) and that which answer fits depends on what the tree is, how close it stands and what the ground is, never that a tree is or is not safe. Never a judgement about the garden's age or state.
cards.mechanism: planting and levels set for an older garden

faq_slots.answer_brief: When each kind of [WORK_LOWER] work is best done and why, in the soil or the plant, from the trade facts timing cells: paving, footings and groundwork wait for ground that is neither frozen nor sodden, because a base cannot be firmed when it is wet; turf, seed and planting go in while the soil is warm and moist so roots take before heat or frost; tree work follows the species and the nest check rather than a season. Nothing about spring being busy or booking ahead. No dates, no promises about the weather.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked. Where the symptom is a seasonal sign (moss through winter, a brown lawn in a drought, early leaf fall), say first when it is normal and then what is not, before anything else. Then the usual cause here in plain words, what the local ground or housing adds, and what the business does about it. One figure at most.

problem_card.title: Damage that shows after a wet winter
problem_card.brief: Say first what is normal at the end of winter: moss on shaded paving, a lawn slow to dry, timber dark with damp, all of which ease as the ground warms and dries. Then what is not: a slab that has lifted, a post that now moves, a step that rocks, a wall with a new crack. The one cause this card makes: frost moving what water had loosened over the winter. Say what gets looked at in spring, from confirmed practices only, and what putting it right involves from the trade facts stages. Nothing about spring being busy or booking ahead.
problem_card.mechanism: frost moving what water had loosened

faq_slot.question: Can you do [WORK_LOWER] work in winter?
faq_slot.answer_brief: What runs in the cold months (hard landscaping in dry spells, clearance, fencing) and what waits (turf and planting while the ground is frozen), with the reason: a base cannot be firmed on frozen or sodden ground, and roots do not take in frozen soil. No dates.

cards.title: A lawn full of moss and bare patches
cards.brief: Say first what is normal: moss in a lawn at the end of a wet winter is usual and thins as the grass starts growing again in spring. Then what is not: moss that holds on through summer, bare patches that never fill. The one cause this card makes: shade and damp ground. The fix is scarifying to lift the moss and overseeding the thin patches, in spring or early autumn while the grass is growing and can recover, linking the lawn care or lawn seeding page where LINKABLE PAGES has one; never mowing alone as the answer, never a promise the moss will not return. On a Lawn care page the card reads as what shows in the lawn, and the season whose treatment answers it: the autumn moss treatment and scarify, the spring feed. Not compaction, not thatch, not the cutting height: other cards and the FAQ own those.
cards.mechanism: shade and damp ground

cards.title: Hedges that have got away
cards.brief: A hedge gone wide at the top and thin at the base, growth over the path. The one cause this card makes: cuts missed or made at the wrong time of year, so the growth went woody. Time of year and the reason: a cut before midsummer, while the season's growth is still soft, keeps the blade out of thick wood; the window differs by species (the trade facts timing cell). The nest check before any cut is a stage of the job in the trade facts; written as this business's own practice only when nesting_bird_check is confirmed. Say what bringing a hedge back involves (a cut in stages over more than one season, never one hard cut) with no promise it will thicken up or recover. On a Lawn care page the card reads as the lawn in a dry summer: grass going brown in a dry spell is normal and greens again with rain (say so first); what is not is grass scalped by a low cut or cut hard after being left, so the height and the timing of cuts are the fix.
cards.mechanism: the timing and height of cuts

cards.title: Weeds that come straight back
cards.brief: Weeds through paving joints and across beds within weeks of clearing. The one cause this card makes: roots left in the ground. Say what dealing with the root involves, from confirmed practices only (weed_roots_out: lifted out with the root); otherwise what stops weeds in general terms, with no promise they stay away. Time of year and the reason: hoeing and lifting while weeds are small in spring, before they set seed and before the roots go deep. On a Lawn care page the card reads as weeds in the lawn that are mown off and come back because the root stays, and the spring or early summer treatment while they are growing (a product only where [CV: materials_methods] gives it). Not bare soil or mulch: the mulching card owns that.
cards.mechanism: roots left in the ground

cards.title: Borders that dry out or get swamped
cards.brief: Beds bare and dry by the first warm week, or sodden all winter. The one cause this card makes: bare soil with nothing covering it. Time of year and the reason: mulch goes on in spring once the soil has warmed and is moist, or in autumn, so it holds the moisture in and keeps the light off weed seedlings; never onto frozen soil. What the round does through the year from confirmed practices only (soil_covered_after_clearance). On a Lawn care page the card reads as bare or thin patches where soil shows through the grass, and overseeding in early autumn or mid spring while the soil is warm and moist so the seed takes. No promise about how the planting or the lawn will come on.
cards.mechanism: bare soil with nothing covering it

problem_card.title: Leaves and debris burying the lawn

problem_card.title: What a winter leaves behind
problem_card.brief: What shows in spring after the cold months, from the trade facts signs row for this job. Say first what is normal after a winter (a green film on timber and paving, ground slow to dry, a lawn thin after the cold) and then what is not. The one cause this card makes: ground heaving and shrinking through the winter. Say what gets looked at in spring from confirmed practices only; otherwise what the job puts right. Not water sitting (card 4) and not a skipped stage (card 2).
problem_card.mechanism: ground heaving and shrinking through the winter

faq_slot.question: When is the best time of year for [SERVICE_LOWER], and how long does it take?
faq_slot.answer_brief: From the trade facts timing row only: the season the job suits and why, in the soil or the plant, then the duration where the row gives one, else what decides it. No dates, no promises about the weather. This is the one place the timing is written.

cards.title: The part of the garden you never use
cards.brief: The customer's situation: a corner, a slope or a stretch of lawn nobody goes to because it is wet, uneven, shaded or bare. What decides it: the ground there (a slope, soil that holds water, a worn patch, a change of level) and how the household wants to use it. What the work gives them, from the trade facts stages for this service: a patio or deck to sit on, a path or steps that make it reachable, a lawn or artificial grass that takes the children, a pond, a pergola or a tree that gives a reason to go down there. Never a fault invented for it, never a lifestyle pitch: the ground and the use, not the dream.
cards.mechanism: ground that is not level, dry or firm enough to use

cards.title: Doing it once, properly
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they have had a cheap quote or thought about doing it themselves, and want to know what the difference buys. What decides it: the layer they will never see once it is finished (the sub base, the subframe and its supports, the footings, the liner, the soil preparation, the planting pit), which is where a quick job cuts corners and where it gives way a winter or two later. What the work gives them: that layer done as the trade facts stages name it, so the surface stays put. One specific from the stages for this service; no depth or figure the rows do not give; never a dig at another trade.
cards.mechanism: the layer underneath, which decides how long it lasts

cards.title: Which option suits your garden
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they are weighing two or three ways of doing it (turf against seed, timber against composite, a patio against a deck, a liner against a preformed pond, natural against artificial grass, a bare root tree against a container grown one). What decides it: the garden's ground, shade, slope and use, and how much looking after they want, from the trade facts materials and methods cell for this service. What the work gives them: the option that suits their garden, never the one that is best in general. A named product only from [CV: materials_methods]. No claim about lifespan or cost unless the rows or the client values give it.
cards.mechanism: the ground, the shade and the use deciding the option

cards.title: What it will need from you afterwards
cards.brief: The customer's situation: they want to know what they are taking on once the job is done. What decides it: what the new surface or plant needs to settle in and then through the year, from the trade facts stages and timing cell for this service (new turf watered and kept off until it has rooted, a young tree watered through its first summers and its stake checked, artificial grass brushed, a pond's pump looked at, timber recoated, paving joints topped up). What the work gives them: an honest picture of what it saves them and what it does not. Never a promise about how it will look or last; a maintenance visit offered only where the services list has one.
cards.mechanism: what the new surface or plant needs to settle in

problem_card.title: Getting it in at the right time of year
problem_card.brief: The customer's situation: they want it ready for the summer, or want to know when it should go in. What decides it: the window the soil or the plant gives, from the trade facts timing cell for this service (turf and seed while the soil is warm and moist; bare root planting in the dormant months; paving and footings when the ground is neither frozen nor sodden; pond planting as the water warms; composite boards at the maker's temperatures). What the work gives them: a job done in its window so it takes. No dates, nothing about spring being busy or booking ahead, no promise about the weather.
problem_card.mechanism: the window the soil or the plant gives

faq_slot.question: When is the best time of year for [SERVICE_LOWER], and how long does it take?
faq_slot.answer_brief: From the trade facts timing row only: the season the job suits and why, in the soil or the plant, then the duration where the row gives one, else what decides it. No dates, no promises about the weather. This is the one place the timing is written.

items.title: Looking over the area first
items.brief: The first stage of a visit from the trade facts: debris, growth, hazards, what has changed since last time. A part of the visit, not a promise.

items.title: Setting the height, line or method
items.brief: The cutting height, the line of the hedge, the treatment chosen: from the trade facts methods cell. A named product only from [CV: materials_methods].

items.title: The main work of the visit
items.brief: The central stage from the trade facts: the mow, the cut, the clearance, the treatment, named as the trade names it.

items.title: Edges, sides and the awkward bits
items.brief: The edging, strimming, the sides and top, the corners a machine cannot reach: from the trade facts stages.

items.title: Collecting what comes off
items.brief: Clippings, arisings, what the visit takes off. Collected or left only from the confirmed practices (clippings_collected, green_waste_choice); otherwise say it is collected or spread as agreed.

items.title: Paths and surfaces cleared before we leave
items.brief: The last stage from the trade facts: paths swept, surfaces cleared, the area left usable.

items.title: The visit pattern you choose
items.brief: Only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; when it is blank, write that visits follow the pattern agreed with you and name no frequency.

included.note: Fallback only: the tick items are the service's own Table A stages when the pack gives 6 or more; this set is used when it gives fewer (F-ITEMS-GENERIC).

problems.h2: Signs It's Time for a [SERVICE] Visit

cards.title: Growth has got ahead of you
cards.brief: The signs from the trade facts signs row: long grass, a hedge over the path, beds overrun. The one cause this card makes: a visit missed in the growing season. Time of year and the reason: from spring to midsummer, once the soil has warmed, growth is at its fastest and a missed visit shows within a fortnight. Then what the visit does, from the stages; what skipping leads to from the skipped row (long grass cut hard is scalped, and the clumps shade what is under them).
cards.mechanism: a visit missed in the growing season

cards.title: It looks untidy from the house
cards.brief: The things that show from a window or the door: grass over the edge of the path, a ragged line against the bed, clumps left on the grass. The one cause this card makes: edge growth creeping over paths and beds between cuts, fastest in late spring when the lawn is growing hardest. Say what the visit puts right (the edge cut back to its line, the clippings collected or spread as agreed) from the stages; no promise it stays that way.
cards.mechanism: edge growth creeping over paths and beds

cards.title: It keeps coming back
cards.brief: Weeds, moss or growth that returns within weeks of a tidy up. Say first when the return is normal (moss at the end of a wet winter where the ground stays damp, a flush of growth after warm rain) and then when it is not (a weed back within weeks of a treatment in the growing season). The one cause this card makes: the cause never dealt with, only what shows. Say what the visit does about the cause, from the trade facts, and the season it is done in (treatments while the plant is growing, in spring or autumn); never a product the client values do not give, never a promise it will not return. Not roots left in the ground, not shade and damp: the category page owns those.
cards.mechanism: the cause never dealt with, only what shows

cards.title: Every cut is a bigger job than the last
cards.brief: The customer's side: a job that takes longer every time it is done. The one cause this card makes: growth that thickens and hardens the longer it is left (grass left long is harder to cut evenly and clumps, hedge growth goes woody by midsummer so a late cut goes into thicker wood, weeds left to seed come back in numbers). Time of year: late spring to midsummer, when growth is fastest. Say what a regular visit changes (a cut kept in soft growth), without a frequency unless [CV: visit_frequency_options] is set, and no promise about the result.
cards.mechanism: growth that thickens and hardens the longer it is left

cards.title: What a visit has to get through
cards.brief: The size and the growth, from the trade facts price row: a larger or awkward area, long or wet growth, more to cut or clear. Say it plainly and give no figure.

cards.title: How much is in the way
cards.brief: Obstacles, slopes, beds to work round, access for the machine, from the trade facts price row. Say why they add time.

cards.title: The first visit
cards.brief: An area left a season needs a first visit that is a bigger job; after that each visit is priced as a visit. Nothing priced on time, no hourly rule, no frequency unless [CV: visit_frequency_options] is set. Not the regular round against a tidy up: the category page owns that.

cards.title: Extras you add to the visit
cards.brief: Work the visit can take on as well, from the sibling service pages and the services list only (an edge, a feed, a hedge, a treatment), and that each adds to the visit. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

steps.title: Tell Us What Needs Keeping On Top Of
steps.brief: How to get in touch and what is useful to send first (the size of the area, what needs doing, photos if they have them). No promise of a reply time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps.title: We Agree the Visit and the Price
steps.brief: What a visit will cover and what it costs. The price agreed before the first visit only when the price_agreed_before_work practice is confirmed. Follows [CV: quote_method]; only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates "free".

steps.title: We Start on a Date That Suits You
steps.brief: The first visit goes in the diary on a day that suits the customer. A regular pattern following on only when the maintenance_schedule practice is confirmed. Never mention the price or changes to the plan.

faq_slots.question: How often should [SERVICE_LOWER] be done?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What decides it, from the trade facts timing row (the growing season, the weather, the species) in plain words, and the season the work runs. A frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; otherwise say the pattern is agreed with you and nothing more. This is the one place the timing is written.

faq_slots.question: How much does a [SERVICE_LOWER] visit cost in [CITY]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise how the price is reached, from [CV: quote_method] only, and that the figure is agreed before the first visit when that practice is confirmed. The four cost cards above already give what moves the price: name one factor at most, never the list again.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured for [SERVICE_LOWER]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers.

faq_slots.question: What if something gets damaged during a visit?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard every trade works to. No promise to put it right free. Never invent a guarantee or insurance.

faq_slots.question: Do I need to be home for a [SERVICE_LOWER] visit?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: access_handling] and the confirmed practices only: whether the customer needs to be in, side gates, keys. When nothing is on file, say the arrangements for getting in are agreed before the first visit and nothing more.

faq_slots.question: What does a [SERVICE_LOWER] visit include?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The What's Included items said as a sentence, in other words. What a visit does not cover only from the services list, with one sibling service page linked.

faq_slots.question: Are there rules or standards for [SERVICE_LOWER]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rule rows only, written as the way the work is usually done, never as something the customer must comply with: a grounds maintenance standard reads as how the job is done, not as homework for the reader. Plain words with "usually" or "in most cases"; what the customer does only where the row says so. Never a standard's number, an Act's name or legal advice. This slot is used only when the service has rule rows.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked. Where the symptom is a seasonal sign (moss through winter, a brown lawn in a drought, early leaf fall), say first when it is normal and then what is not, before anything else. Then the usual cause here in plain words and what a regular visit does about it, in its season. One figure at most.

problem_card.title: What the season is about to throw at it
problem_card.brief: The growth or the fall that comes all at once: spring growth as the soil warms, autumn leaves, as the trade facts timing row has it for this work. Say first that the flush is the season doing what it does, not a fault. The one cause this card makes: growth that comes all at once in spring. Say what getting ahead of it looks like, from the stages; no frequency unless [CV: visit_frequency_options] is set; no promise about the result.
problem_card.mechanism: growth that comes all at once in spring

faq_slot.question: When should [SERVICE_LOWER] start for the year?
faq_slot.answer_brief: When the first visit of the year should happen and the reason in the plant or the ground, from the trade facts timing cell: mowing and hedge work once growth has started as the soil warms; feeds, seeding and renovation while the soil is warm and moist; mulching before the beds have filled out. No dates, no promise of a slot, nothing about booking ahead or a rush. The frequency question owns the season the work runs: do not repeat it.

cards.title: Ground that holds the rain
cards.brief: Lawns soft for days, beds that sit wet, water lying at the bottom of a slope. The one cause this card makes: the ground under the town's gardens holding water; the town profile and a symptom say which ground (clay, a high water table, a river valley, a flood setting). Say what it means for any job that goes into the ground, in plain words; never promise the ground will change. Not a surface laid with no fall, not a base left loose, not water the surface failed to shed: the town's category and service pages own those.
cards.mechanism: the ground under the town's gardens holding water

cards.title: Boundaries as old as the houses
cards.brief: Panels that lean, posts soft at the base, a garden wall with a bow in it. The one cause this card makes: fences and walls put up when the houses were built, which the town profile dates. Tie the era to what replacing a boundary involves, never to a judgement on its state: a run of that age comes out with its posts and their concrete and new holes are dug (the trade facts stages); an old wall's footing was built for that wall and not a higher one; where the boundary is shared, the neighbour usually has to be told first ("usually", never an Act's name). What the business does only from confirmed practices. Not timber in wet ground, not a repair that no longer holds: other pages own those.
cards.mechanism: fences and walls put up when the houses were built

cards.title: Trees that have outgrown the garden
cards.brief: Roots lifting a path, a canopy over the whole lawn, leaves in every gutter. The one cause this card makes: trees planted when the garden was bigger, or the house further away, than it is now (never the word plot: it is on the words to avoid list); the town profile gives the mature trees, the conservation areas, the tree protection. What usually applies before a protected tree is touched, with "usually" and never an order's name. Not shade on a lawn: the Gardener pages own that.
cards.mechanism: trees planted for a bigger garden than there is now

cards.title: Front gardens turned over to parking
cards.brief: A paved front that sends rain to the road or next door, a dropped kerb with nothing to soak the water. The one cause this card makes: rain running off a paved front with nowhere to soak in. What usually applies to a new hard surface at the front (a permeable surface, or a drain inside the garden), in plain words, never the rule's name; where the town profile gives the street pattern (terraces with no drive), say what it means. Not water on a patio: the service pages own that.
cards.mechanism: rain running off a paved front

cost.h2: What Affects the Cost of [WORK] in [TOWN]

cards.title: Getting in on a terraced street
cards.brief: Where the back garden can be got to only through the house or by a shared side path, materials come in by hand and deliveries and waste wait on the road. Say why that adds time (never "the only way": a superlative); the town profile says which streets are terraced. No figure.

cards.title: Gardens on a slope
cards.brief: A garden that falls or rises from the house needs levels taken, steps or a retaining edge, and more digging than a flat garden. Say it plainly, from the town profile where it gives the slope. No figure.

cards.title: Conservation areas and protected trees
cards.brief: Where the town has conservation areas or tree protection, the checks and the paperwork before work can start add time, and some things cannot be done at all. "Usually", never the order's or the area's official name. From the dossier rules only; otherwise a tree survey as something that sometimes applies.

cards.title: What the last owner left behind
cards.brief: Old concrete, a shed base, buried rubble, an overgrown hedge: what has to come out and be taken away before anything new goes in. What the town's housing era usually left in the ground, from the profile only (an old path under the lawn, a coal bunker base), said as what the work meets and never as a judgement on the gardens. How it is taken away only from confirmed practices. No figure.

faq_slots.question: How much does [WORK_LOWER] cost in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise the things that push the price up in a town like this (access, slope, what has to come out) and how the quote is given, from [CV: quote_method] only.

faq_slots.question: How soon can you get to [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] and [CV: response_time] only. The town is in the area covered; nothing about distance unless [CV: travel_distance] is set.

faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes: the town and the villages around it (code lists them; name none). How the business reaches it from its base only from the client values. Link one page in this town.

faq_slots.answer_brief: Start with yes, then the terms from [CV: guarantee_years] and [CV: guarantee_scope]. Described, never promised.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something isn't right after the job?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard every trade works to. No promise to come back free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: What happens when I ask for a quote in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] and the confirmed practices only: what the customer sends, what the business looks at, what comes back. No timescale unless [CV: response_time] is set.

faq_slots.question: When is the best time of year for [WORK_LOWER] work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: When each kind of [WORK_LOWER] work is best done and why, in the soil or the plant, from the trade facts timing cells: paving, footings and groundwork wait for ground that is neither frozen nor sodden, because a base cannot be firmed when it is wet; turf, seed and planting go in while the soil is warm and moist so roots take before heat or frost. Where the town profile gives the ground (clay still wet in spring, sand dry by June), say what it does to that window. Nothing about spring being busy or booking ahead. No dates, no promises about the weather.

cards.title: Lawns that struggle on this ground
cards.brief: Grass that goes brown in the first dry week, or stays mossy all winter. Say first what is normal (browning in a dry spell that greens again with rain, moss at the end of a wet winter that thins as growth starts) and then what is not (a lawn thin all year, moss holding on through summer). The one cause this card makes: the soil under the town's lawns (the profile: fast draining gravel, heavy clay, a river valley). What a regular round does about it in plain words and in its season (the height of cut in a dry spell, an autumn feed, scarifying or aerating in spring or autumn where it fits); anything the business itself promises only from confirmed practices; never a promise the lawn will stay green. Not shade and damp ground: the Gardener pages own that.
cards.mechanism: the soil under the town's lawns

cards.title: Hedges as old as the houses
cards.brief: Hedges planted when the street was built, now mature. Name a species only where the town profile gives it; otherwise "the hedges". The one cause this card makes: hedges planted with the houses, now carrying a lot of old wood. What the hedge's age means for the work, never a judgement on how it looks: thick wood at the base that is cut back in stages over more than one season rather than in one hard cut, at the species' time of year, with the nest check before each cut (a stage of the job in the trade facts). No promise it will thicken or recover. Not the timing of cuts: the Gardener pages own that.
cards.mechanism: hedges planted with the houses, now full of old wood

cards.title: Gardens that run away in the growing season
cards.brief: A garden tidy in April and lost by July. The one cause this card makes: the town's ground pushing growth on fast once the soil warms (the profile: rich or moist soil, a sheltered valley, heavy ground that holds water into summer). Never who lives here. What a regular round keeps on top of through late spring and summer, from the card list; a frequency only from the confirmed practices; no promise about the result.
cards.mechanism: the town's ground pushing growth on fast in spring

cards.title: A garden that came with the house
cards.brief: New owners with planting they do not know, a lawn cut the wrong way for a season, beds left to see what comes up. The one cause this card makes: a garden inherited with the house (the profile: a new estate where the lawn is turf over compacted builder's ground, or an older garden with established planting and old hedges). What a first visit sorts out and what waits a season to see what comes up; promises only from confirmed practices. Never that the owner has neglected it, never a judgement on the previous one.
cards.mechanism: a garden inherited with the house

cards.title: Getting the mower round the back
cards.brief: Terraced streets with no side gate mean the mower and the waste go through the house. Say why that adds time to a visit, from the profile where it gives the housing.

cards.title: A garden that has been left a while
cards.brief: The first visit on a garden that has had a season or two off is a bigger job than the round that follows. Say it plainly; no figure; not the service pages' first visit card in the same words.

cards.title: Banks and sloping lawns
cards.brief: A lawn on a bank is cut with a different machine and takes longer; steps and terraces add edges. From the profile where the town has slopes.

cards.title: Big hedges and old trees
cards.brief: A mature hedge takes longer each cut, and some trees are a tree surgeon's job, not the gardener's. Say which work moves to the tree pages only where LINKABLE PAGES has one in this town.

faq_slots.question: What does a regular [WORK_LOWER] round cost in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise how the price is reached, from [CV: quote_method] only, and that the figure is agreed before the first visit when that practice is confirmed. One factor at most, never the list again.

faq_slots.question: How soon can you get to [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] and [CV: response_time] only. The town is in the area covered; nothing about distance unless [CV: travel_distance] is set.

faq_slots.question: Do you cover [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes: the town and the villages around it (code lists them; name none). How the business reaches it from its base only from the client values. Link one page in this town.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured for garden work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something gets broken on a visit?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard. No promise to put it right free. Never invent a guarantee or insurance.

faq_slots.question: How do regular visits work in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the confirmed practices only: whether the customer needs to be in, keys, how the visit is agreed. A frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]. Never promise a schedule.

faq_slots.question: Do you garden through the winter in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What the round does in each season in plain words (cutting through the growing season, clearing and pruning in the cold months). No dates.

cards.title: A garden with nowhere to sit out
cards.brief: A situation card, not a fault: the household looks at the garden from the house and has nowhere flat and dry for a table and chairs, to let the children out or to stand with a coffee. What decides it: the levels and the ground by the back door (a slope, a lawn that stays wet, a step down to nothing). What the work gives them, in plain words: a patio or a deck made the size they will use, a level lawn, steps that make the lower garden reachable. By category: Paving reads it as the patio and its base; Decking as the deck, where the evening sun falls and what holds it up; Landscape Gardener as whichever fits the garden; Tree Service as the one sunny corner shaded out by a tree that has grown over it, and what lifting or thinning the crown gives back. Never a lifestyle pitch, never a fault invented for it.
cards.mechanism: no level, dry place to sit near the house

cards.title: Slabs and blocks that rock or have sunk
cards.mechanism: a sub base too thin or too soft for what sits on it
cards.brief: A slab that rocks when it is stepped on, a line of blocks that has dipped by the drain, a joint that has opened: the sub base under it was never compacted or was too thin for the ground. Say the fix starts underneath (the area lifted, the base made good, the slabs or blocks relaid), from the trade facts stages; no depth, no figure, and nothing about boards or posts.

cards.title: Rain that stays where it lands
cards.brief: Problem led: puddles that sit on paving after rain, a deck green and slippery by autumn, a corner of lawn soft for days, a planting hole that fills with water. The one cause this card makes: a surface laid with no fall, so the rain cannot run off it. Say what the fix usually involves (a fall built into the laying, a base that drains, timber kept off wet ground, a tree planted at the right level) from the trade facts stages; what the business does on site only from confirmed practices. Never promise the ground will change. By category: Paving reads it on the surface; Decking in boards and joists that never dry; Tree Service in a tree standing in ground that holds water; Landscape Gardener across the garden. Not slow draining ground on its own: the symptom FAQ may own that.
cards.mechanism: a surface laid with no fall

cards.title: Planted or built for a different garden
cards.brief: A situation and a warning sign in one: borders now hard against the path, a drive too small for the cars that use it, a deck in the corner the sun left years ago, a tree planted close to the house that now reaches the roof. The one cause this card makes: planting and levels set years ago for a different garden. Say how looking at the whole garden before pricing one part of it works, from confirmed practices only. By category: Landscape Gardener reads it as layout and levels; Paving as the front garden and the drive; Decking as a platform in the wrong place or at the wrong height; Tree Service as the warning signs in the tree itself (branches rubbing the building, deadwood showing, a damaged limb, from the trade facts signs row) and that which answer fits depends on what the tree is, how close it stands and what the ground is, never that a tree is or is not safe. Never a judgement about the garden's age or state.
cards.mechanism: planting and levels set for an older garden

cost.h2: What Affects the Cost of [WORK] in [CITY]

cards.title: The size of the area
cards.brief: Square metres move the price more than anything else: more digging, more sub base, more slabs or blocks, more days. Say it plainly and give no figure.

cards.title: What is underneath
cards.brief: Topsoil, clay, an old slab base or concrete that has to come out before a new sub base goes in: the dig and the waste set the number of days. Say the business looks before it prices, from [CV: quote_method] only.

cards.title: Getting to the garden
cards.brief: Rear access, a path down the side, where a skip can sit and how far the sub base and the slabs are carried by hand. Say why a tight access costs more time.

cards.title: The slabs or blocks you choose
cards.brief: Natural stone against concrete slabs against porcelain, block paving against slabs, and the bed and the edging each needs: a porcelain slab wants a primed full bed, blocks want a compacted laying course and a kerb to hold them. Name a material only if the trade facts or [CV: materials_methods] give it; nothing here about timber, decking or fencing. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.
